source.title: The period-index problem for real surfaces
source.version: Published 48-page version; all pages read. ArXiv v2 and author copy used only for targeted cross-checks.
source.versionChecks: Published pp.76,84,85 visually checked. Author and arXiv v2 retain the coefficient expressions in Proposition4.5. No claim that all versions are textually identical.

summary: A Hodge-theoretic proof of period=index for real-surface Brauer classes vanishing at every real point, and an exact topological obstruction for unramified classes on smooth projective real surfaces. Applications compute the Elman–Lam u-invariant in transcendence degree two, real Enriques cases and a non-archimedean real-closed counterexample. This is a full-main-paper reading checkpoint, not proof closure: source-typing gates in §§4 and 7 and unread prerequisite proof interiors remain.

conventions.base: R means the actual real numbers except where explicitly replaced by an arbitrary real closed field. A smooth connected projective R-surface need not be geometrically connected. H^i(Y) without coefficients means F2-cohomology.
conventions.G: G=Gal(C/R)=C2 with generator conjugation σ; H_G denotes Borel/Grothendieck equivariant sheaf cohomology, not merely invariants of ordinary cohomology.
conventions.twists: Benoist uses Z(j)=i^j Z with σ=(-1)^j; parity determines its G-module. Identify with the 2πi normalization in Benoist2018 by an explicit rescaling, not literal equality of embedded lattices.
conventions.Brauer: For smooth integral X use Br(X)=H²_et(X,G_m), torsion here by injection into Br(k(X)). Field algebraic/cohomological comparison is a separate imported theorem. Multiplicative Lean Brauer identity 1 corresponds to additive paper 0.
conventions.status: library describes only the precisely stated sub-item, planned only the named current layer's scope, missing is relative to the pinned baseline and catalogue snapshot. A route is a design proposal, not an implemented theorem.

items.name: Period-index arithmetic
items.statement: For any field K and α∈Br(K), per(α) divides ind(α) and the two have the same prime divisors.

items.name: Index under extension

items.statement: For characteristic-zero K, u(K) is the supremum in N∪{∞} of dimensions of anisotropic forms whose signatures vanish at every field ordering.
